title: Replit Agent Skills: SKILL.md Structure and Scoping Discipline
content:
# Customize Replit Agent with Skills and Custom Instructions

Published June 2026.

## Custom Instructions

Always-on guidelines automatically injected into the agent's context across all projects. Workspace Settings → Customization. Available to **Pro and Enterprise** users — broader than the Enterprise-only design systems feature, so Pro users can approximate design system constraint through instructions alone.

## Skills

Activate conditionally when relevant tasks arise: "a skill only kicks in when a relevant task comes up."

Each skill is a folder containing SKILL.md plus supporting files. The main file has three components:

1. **Name** — short, lowercase identifier (e.g. api-design)
2. **Description** — determines when the agent uses the skill; **should specify when *not* to use it**
3. **Instructions** — rules, patterns, and things to avoid, in any format

The guidance that a description should state when *not* to fire is directly relevant to design systems: a design-system skill with an overbroad description will load on backend tasks, waste context, or crowd out a more specific skill.

## How skills load

- Automatically based on prompt relevance
- Manually via /skill-name syntax
- Selected from the "+" menu button

Manual /skill-name invocation matters for reliability — practitioners who find the skill isn't auto-firing can force it.

## The scoping principle, verbatim

**"Small, well-scoped skills combine cleanly. A skill that tries to cover everything tends to crowd out the skills that should have fired instead."**

This argues against one monolithic design-system skill and for splitting by concern — tokens, layout patterns, component APIs, accessibility — consistent with the references/guides/ and references/components/ subdivision in Replit's design system docs.

## Design system skill example

A design-system skill fires when someone builds UI, ensuring consistency across projects. The stated benefit: "the agent builds UI that fits your product, not a slightly different interpretation every time" — a concise statement of the drift problem every AI generator is attacking.
